prompts.task: Add OpenTelemetry instrumentation to the Go key-value store service in ./service. Assume no custom business spans are requested.
Instrument the Go key-value store service in ./service with OpenTelemetry while preserving the existing runtime and startup command. Add auto-instrumentation only; do not add custom business spans.

judge_inputs: Inspect ./service for resulting files when present.
Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response.
rubric:
Rule: Instrument the server executable under cmd/kvstore-server.
Example: Telemetry starts with the server command, not when another program imports kvstore.
Evidence: Inspect the command entrypoint and initialization order.
Insufficient evidence: Instrumentation added only to the library package or activated by importing it.

Rule: Preserve the existing kvstore package APIs and business logic.
Example: Adding telemetry leaves the store operations in their existing package.
Evidence: Compare the package interfaces and application changes with the baseline.
Insufficient evidence: Moving business logic or changing package APIs to fit instrumentation.

Rule: Use otelhttp.NewHandler for the stdlib HTTP routes and keep span names low-cardinality.
Example: Use a stable handler name rather than a key taken from a request.
Evidence: Inspect the handler wrapper and resulting span names.
Insufficient evidence: Manual HTTP wiring that omits otelhttp or span names containing unbounded request values.

Rule: Read service name and OTLP destination from the environment, with safe defaults.
Example: An operator can change OTEL_SERVICE_NAME without editing Go source.
Evidence: Inspect the consumed configuration and exporter setup.
Insufficient evidence: Hardcoded identity or destination that ignores the supported environment settings.

Rule: Bridge the existing standard logger through one official Go bridge and one shared-resource, batched OTLP LoggerProvider. Default its signal-specific logs route to local Splunk Observability Studio.
Example: A standard-log call keeps its original console sink and reaches the single log pipeline.
Evidence: Inspect bridge/provider ownership, shared Resource, batch processor and /v1/logs destination.
Insufficient evidence: A second bridge/provider, an unbatched replacement, or loss of the original logger.

Rule: Export each request-context warning exactly once with its body, WARN severity, the effective service.name from the shared Resource and unique nonempty trace/span IDs. Preserve the standard-log console sink.
Example: Two requests produce separate correlated warnings without duplicate exported copies.
Evidence: Inspect received warning fields and counts, and confirm the original console output remains.
Insufficient evidence: Missing or duplicate warnings, missing required fields or IDs, or a replaced console sink.

Rule: Honor OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=none and other explicit operator-owned exporters. Add no local LoggerProvider or bridge on those branches.
Example: The none branch leaves standard-log output usable.
Evidence: Inspect the effective exporter branch and local provider/bridge construction, with original console output retained.
Insufficient evidence: Adding a local pipeline despite the selection or disabling the original sink.

Rule: Resolve the approved local logs receiver for the selected runtime before applying the setup. Preserve approved signal-specific local headers for the official exporter to parse.
Example: Port 55319 conflicts with an approved port 55318; valid local-log headers alone do not.
Evidence: Use signal-specific or compatible generic configuration, receiver status or checked-in launch/Compose evidence. Use the 127.0.0.1:4318/v1/logs fallback only when none exists. An explicit logs URL must match the approved host, port and path. Nonempty generic headers, true endpoint/protocol conflicts or exporter setup failure skip only added logs, with a value-free diagnostic; application, native logs, traces and metrics continue. Preserve operator settings rather than masking local headers with an empty override.
Insufficient evidence: Approving any loopback URL, rejecting valid local headers, leaking generic credentials, or stopping unrelated startup for a safely isolated log conflict.

Rule: Keep added application-log export local, with no cloud log endpoint, credential, exporter or forwarding path. Preserve explicit operator-owned log routes. Direct cloud remains trace/metric-only.
Example: Direct-cloud trace and metric settings remain separate from local application logs.
Evidence: Inspect generic and signal-specific destinations, headers and forwarding configuration.
Insufficient evidence: Copying cloud configuration into the added log path or silently replacing an operator-owned route.

Rule: Use one shutdown path on every normal or signal-driven server exit so the single log provider and batch processor flush once.
Example: A signal reaches the existing server lifecycle and then the same telemetry finalizer.
Evidence: Inspect normal/signal exit paths and their shutdown checks.
Insufficient evidence: An exit that skips flushing or calls the log-provider shutdown more than once.

Rule: Update the existing .vscode/launch.json as required by the loaded skill.
Example: The existing debug launch consumes the selected instrumentation configuration.
Evidence: Compare the saved debug configuration with the implemented startup settings.
Insufficient evidence: Leaving a required launch update stale or replacing it with unrelated startup instructions.
